subject.title: [Feature]: support SecretRef for channel phone numbers as it's Personal Identifiable Information (PII)

question: Should OpenClaw treat channel phone numbers, sender identifiers, and allowlists as SecretRef-capable sensitive config across bundled messaging and telephony plugins, with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/73822 as the canonical implementation path?
rationale: This changes security-sensitive config semantics and access-control inputs across several channel/plugin surfaces, so automation should not choose the permanent policy or scope without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use the open linked PR as the implementation path, requiring security, compatibility, and real-runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the scope first
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that starts with the highest-risk supported channels and tracks remaining channel coverage separately.

options.title: Defer phone identifiers
options.body: Keep SecretRef support limited to credentials for now and document the plaintext phone-number tradeoff until maintainers approve a broader sensitive-identifier policy.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use the open linked PR as the implementation path, requiring security, compatibility, and real-runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest overlap across the issue discussion, WhatsApp/SMS config history, and SecretRef documentation surface.
